meta.location: Hilton Head Island, South Carolina, USA

primary_study_window.rationale: Stable Harbour Town RBC Heritage setup in the ShotLink era with consistent par-71 configuration and broadly similar conditioning pre-2024 restoration.

renovation_windows.label: Post-restoration
renovation_windows.description: Love Golf Design restoration and 2025 reopening with rebuilt bunkers, restored edges, selective tree moves, and renewed turf/irrigation.
renovation_windows.likely_effects: Preserves short positional identity with tiny greens; slightly sharper visual framing and marginally higher effective penalty on some lines, but no material change in par, yardage, or core DNA.
renovation_windows.comparability_rule: Treat 2024+ as structurally comparable to 2004–2023 for macro traits but tag as post-restoration and weight at 0.75 in trait evidence windows until enough post-reno data is audited.

excluded_years.reason: Pre-full ShotLink and less reliable strokes-gained and per-hole trait data.

partially_comparable_years.rule: Use for directional trait evidence (approach, tight OTT, Bermuda putting) with 0.75 weight relative to 2004–2023 until post-renovation audits support equal weighting.

green_surface.description: Tiny, quick Bermuda greens with modest internal contour and tightly mown grainy surrounds.
green_surface.implications: Approach proximity and short-game precision are amplified; poor distance control and short-siding are punished.

wind_exposure.description: Mostly tree-sheltered interior with significantly exposed coastal stretch on 16–18, especially 17–18 alongside Calibogue Sound.
wind_exposure.pattern: Wind direction and speed materially affect par-3s and the closing stretch, creating high leverage holes in moderate to strong wind.

elevation_profile.description: Very flat coastal terrain with minimal elevation changes and mostly level lies.
elevation_profile.implications: No altitude distance boost; tests are directional control, trajectory, and wind management rather than uphill/downhill adjustments.

rough_severity.description: Thin, modest Bermuda rough; lies are generally playable, but trees, water, and angles are the real penalty.
rough_severity.implications: Fairway vs rough is more about angle and access to small greens than pure lie quality; blocked drives are far more costly than standard rough misses.

driving_corridor_tightness.description: Very tight, tree-lined corridors with overhanging limbs and water/lagoons on multiple holes; many tee shots play through narrow chutes.
driving_corridor_tightness.implications: Rewards positional drivers with high fairway retention and comfort clubbing down; penalizes extreme distance profiles that miss in the wrong places.

par5_reachability.description: Shorter par-5s where much of the field can reach in two, but with constrained corridors and tree interference.
par5_reachability.implications: Par-5 scoring matters, but it is more about smart layup positions and precise long-approach control than raw carry distance.

pressure_holes.definition: Holes with polarized scoring distributions (birdie/bogey or worse) and high leverage on the leaderboard, especially under wind.
identified_sets: Longer par-3s (~190–200 yards) with shifting wind directions.
Closing stretch 16–18, especially 17 (par-3) and 18 (long par-4 along water and OB).
pressure_holes.implications: Maintaining neutral or positive strokes-gained on these holes strongly correlates with top finishes.

routing_bias.description: Pete Dye routing and tree overhangs reward players who can work both left-to-right and right-to-left; no clear aggregate draw or fade bias.

winning_score_band.description: Medium-scoring venue where wind and firmness drive volatility; calm years can push scores into the low 20s under par.

firmness.description: Generally firm-fast with quick greens and tight surrounds, particularly in typical April conditions.
firmness.implications: Approach distance control and spin management are heavily rewarded; approaches that land pin-high with correct trajectories create big edges.

wind_sensitivity.description: High; scoring spread and difficulty scale sharply with wind, especially on exposed par-3s and closing holes.
wind_sensitivity.implications: Ball-flight and trajectory control with mid- to long-irons is critical; wave draw can meaningfully skew round-to-round scoring.

traits.name: SG_Approach
traits.evidence_window: 2004–2023 RBC Heritage full-field SG splits; 2024–2025 included at 0.75 weight
traits.why_it_matters_here: Tiny Bermuda greens and firm conditions make Harbour Town a second-shot course; top finishers consistently rank in the top quartile for SG:APP and proximity.

traits.name: SG_OTT_TightPenalty
traits.evidence_window: 2004–2023 SG:OTT on narrow/penalty holes at Harbour Town; 2024–2025 at 0.75 weight
traits.why_it_matters_here: Narrow, tree-lined corridors and water/OB mean keeping tee shots in play and on the correct side of the fairway strongly drives scoring; uncontrolled distance underperforms.

traits.name: Putting_Bermuda_SurfaceSpecific
traits.evidence_window: 2004–2023 Harbour Town SG:Putting plus similar TifEagle Bermuda venues with conversion; 2024–2025 at 0.75 weight
traits.why_it_matters_here: Small, quick TifEagle greens and subtle grain reward above-average Bermuda putters who can convert frequent mid-range looks and save pars from tight surrounds.

traits.name: Par5_Scoring_GIR_in_2
traits.evidence_window: 2004–2023 par-5 scoring and GIR-in-two vs finishing position; 2024–2025 at 0.75 weight
traits.why_it_matters_here: Short but demanding par-5s are key scoring opportunities; gaining strokes here via smart positioning and precise long-approach play supports high finishes.

traits.name: PressureHole_Scoring
traits.evidence_window: 2004–2023 scoring dispersion and SG on long par-3s and holes 16–18 vs final position
traits.why_it_matters_here: Wind-exposed par-3s and the coastal finish create large swings; players who avoid big numbers and gain on these holes are over-represented among top finishers.

traits.name: Trajectory_ShotShaping_Control
traits.evidence_window: 2004–2023 SG and proximity on forced-shape/dogleg holes at Harbour Town and similar Dye tests
traits.why_it_matters_here: The routing demands both directions and specific windows under trees; players with better shot-shaping and trajectory control score better on these forced-shape holes.

anti_patterns.anti_pattern_name: High-distance / low-accuracy driver with mediocre small-green approach

definition.approach_profile: Below-average proximity on sub-175-yard approaches and on small targets

anti_patterns.historical_evidence: Long, inaccurate drivers with mediocre wedge/mid-iron small-target control repeatedly underperform at Harbour Town despite strong global SG profiles.
anti_patterns.evidence_note: Aligns with historic leaderboards and v2 intake guidance that bomb-and-gouge is structurally disfavored at this venue.

anti_patterns.anti_pattern_name: Elite tee-to-green, consistently negative on Bermuda
anti_patterns.historical_evidence: Players who are elite tee-to-green but consistently lose strokes on Bermuda tend to leak value on Harbour Town’s small, fast TifEagle surfaces.
anti_patterns.evidence_note: Surface-specific pattern supported by broader Bermuda data; penalty size flagged for post-2026 audit.

anti_patterns.anti_pattern_name: Single-shot-shape dependence with poor forced-shape performance

definition.shape_profile: Strong performance when routing favors preferred shape; significant loss on opposite-shape and forced-shape doglegs.
definition.proximity_pattern: Weak proximity and SG on holes requiring opposite curvature from typical pattern.

anti_patterns.historical_evidence: Dye routing and tree framing reward two-way shaping; one-shape-only profiles struggle to access select pins and fairway windows.
anti_patterns.evidence_note: Conceptually strong but requires more granular per-hole data; penalty is intentionally modest pending further audits.

debut_penalty_model.rationale: Tight visuals, tree-lined chutes, small targets, and a wind-exposed finish create a steep learning curve where first-timers often underperform relative to global form.

list.shared_dna: Short par-70/71, positional, tree-lined, coastal wind-exposed, Bermuda greens, emphasis on accuracy and wedge/short-iron approach play.
list.non_translating_elements: Less visually constrictive off the tee and more driver-friendly; different green complexes and contours.

list.shared_dna: Short, positional, tree-lined layout with accuracy focus, wedge/short-iron scoring, and Bermuda putting importance.
list.non_translating_elements: Inland, less wind-affected; larger greens and different pressure-hole mix.

list.shared_dna: Coastal, wind-exposed, positional golf with Bermuda greens; emphasis on iron control and short game.
list.non_translating_elements: More open visuals and less claustrophobic tree framing; different dogleg and hole mix.

list.shared_dna: Shorter venue deemphasizing raw power and rewarding placement plus approach quality with some pressure-hole dynamics.
list.non_translating_elements: Different putting surface, inland winds, and stadium framing; not a Bermuda coastal analog.

comp_courses.combined_comp_influence_rule: Sum of all positive comp adjustments cannot exceed +6 VTS; sum of all negative adjustments cannot exceed -6 VTS for any player.
comp_courses.translation_notes: Apply comp influence only on overlapping traits (accuracy, approach, wind management, and surface-appropriate putting). Surface differences must respect the putting conversion rule.

putting_surface_conversion.primary_rule: If player has >=24 recent rounds on Bermuda, use Bermuda-only SG:Putting as the Harbour Town putting input.
putting_surface_conversion.mapping_to_vts: Convert strokes-per-round surplus/deficit from the blended putting metric into a z-score vs field, then scale into the 0–100 putting sub-score used by the 15% putting weight.
putting_surface_conversion.rationale: Avoid assuming full transfer of putting strength across surfaces; non-Bermuda samples are discounted and blended for a conservative estimate on TifEagle Bermuda.

trait_layer_construction.scaling_rule: Convert each trait into a z-score vs field using ~12-month filtered windows, then map to 0–100 and weight by the trait_weight_matrix.

recent_form_layer.injury_exclusion_rule: Remove starts identified as injury-affected or non-representative before calculating decayed form.
recent_form_layer.form_to_vts_mapping: Convert quality-adjusted, decayed SG:T2G + putting (with Bermuda conversion) into 0–100 form_score and apply the recent_form_weight from venue_history_weights.

comps_blending.application: Compute comp-based trait adjustments per course, sum them while respecting each course cap, then add the net comp_adjustment to the base VTS.
comps_blending.order_of_operations: Apply comp_adjustment after blending venue history, trait matrix, and recent form; before debut and anti-pattern penalties.

debut_and_anti_pattern_penalties.apply_debut_to: Players with zero prior competitive rounds at Harbour Town.
debut_and_anti_pattern_penalties.application_order: Start from base VTS (venue history + traits + form + comps), subtract debut penalty if applicable, subtract all triggered anti-pattern penalties capped at -18, then assign tiers.

health_gate.rule: Players with active injury concerns cannot be Tier 1 or 2 pre-R1 regardless of computed VTS.
health_gate.unlock_condition: Once Round 1 SG and normalized score are consistent with healthy baseline, remove the gate and allow free tiering.

tier_1.name: Course Architects
tier_1.constraints: No active health gate; at most one minor anti-pattern (<7 VTS points).

tier_2.name: Primary Contenders
tier_2.constraints: Moderate anti-pattern penalties allowed (<=12 VTS points); acceptable risk profile.

wave_and_conditions_normalization.method: Compute per-wave scoring average and adjust each player’s raw score by wave baseline to get a normalized score; compare to tier band using normalized value.

downgrade_triggers.condition: Tier 1 or 2 player is >3 shots worse than bottom of normalized expected band AND shows trait failure.

trait_failures.sg_approach: Loses >=1.0 SG:APP vs field in R1.
trait_failures.sg_ott_tight: Loses >=0.75 SG:OTT on tight/penalty holes vs field in R1.
trait_failures.pressure_holes: Loses >=1.0 SG on pressure-hole set (long par-3s and 16–18) vs field in R1.

downgrade_actions.tier_1: Downgrade to Tier 2 or 3 depending on severity.
downgrade_actions.tier_2: Downgrade to Tier 3 or 4 depending on severity.

promotion_triggers.condition: Tier 3–5 player is >=3 shots better than the top of their normalized expected band AND shows strong trait expression.

trait_requirements.sg_approach: Positive SG:APP vs field in R1.
trait_requirements.sg_ott_tight: Positive SG:OTT on tight/penalty holes vs field in R1.
trait_requirements.pressure_holes: Non-negative SG on pressure-hole set in R1.

promotion_triggers.promotion_action: Promote one tier after recomputing VTS with R1 included.
